en: Pagodas to Beilin: Follow the Written Word
zh: 雁塔到碑林：沿着文字走
ja: 雁塔から碑林へ：文字をたどる

p.src: At the Big Wild Goose Pagoda, the eye climbs the brick eaves. At the Small Wild Goose Pagoda, the damaged summit registers first. In Beilin, the gaze drops to columns cut into stone. These are not parts of one museum, and no intact Tang street joins them. What connects them is a sequence: words move between languages, enter durable material, then travel beyond their original room. This chapter follows translation, inscription and circulation rather than ranking three famous monuments.

p.src: When Xuanzang returned to Chang'an in 645, scripture translation was not a solitary performance at one desk. Historical accounts distinguish people who checked Sanskrit and doctrine, shaped the Chinese wording, recorded discussion, collated drafts and prepared fair copies. Personnel and procedure varied between projects, but the image of Xuanzang replacing Sanskrit words with Chinese characters by himself is inadequate. Beneath the pagoda, see him first as the scholar-monk directing collaborative work; the celebrated journey then reconnects with the intellectual institution that received it.

p.src: The first pagoda at Da Ci'en Temple was built in 652 to house and protect scriptures, images and relics brought back by Xuanzang. The seven-storey brick tower now standing incorporates later rebuilding and repair; its visible fabric is not all untouched work from 652. At the south portal, a second chain of making appears. Emperor Taizong and Emperor Gaozong composed paired texts, Chu Suiliang supplied the calligraphy, and craftsmen cut it into stone. Separate authorship, handwriting and carving before admiring the brush forms: the architecture did more than store texts; it staged their preservation and authority.

caption.zh: 从大慈恩寺院内看大雁塔：七层方形砖塔逐层收分，近看比广场上的远望更显厚重。先看整体轮廓，再到南门洞两侧读碑。
caption.ja: 大慈恩寺境内から見る大雁塔。七層の方形煉瓦塔は上へ行くほど細くなり、広場からの遠望より量感が伝わる。まず全体の輪郭を見てから、南の入口両側の碑文へ進む。
caption.en: The Big Wild Goose Pagoda from within Da Ci'en Temple: the square seven-storey brick tower narrows as it rises and feels more massive up close than from the plaza. Read its full silhouette before approaching the paired inscriptions at the south portal.

p.src: Do not treat the Small Wild Goose Pagoda as a reduced Big Pagoda. Construction began in 707 at Jianfu Temple, associated with a separate translation programme led by Yijing; its dense-eaved profile also differs from the Big Pagoda's pavilion form. Originally fifteen levels, it now retains thirteen, with earthquake damage and repair written into the missing summit. An older guide explains a closing crack through a hemispherical rammed-earth foundation and calls it a miracle. Official heritage records confirm damage and the 1964 repair, but do not establish that engineering story. Visible loss needs no invented solution.

p.src: All three points share one scale. The two pagodas stand south of today's wall, while Beilin sits just inside its southern side; all three fall within the generalized Sui-Tang outer city. The dashed joins give this chapter's south-to-north reading order. They are not a walking path, transit line or evidence for Tang streets. Choose two for a half-day: compare translation institutions and tower forms at the pagodas, or connect translation to inscription at the Small Pagoda and Beilin. Give all three a full day.

caption.zh: 大雁塔、小雁塔与碑林使用同一比例。隋唐外郭城范围经过概化，虚线是章节次序，不是步行、公交或唐代道路。
caption.ja: 大雁塔、小雁塔、碑林を同じ縮尺で示す。隋唐外郭城は概略範囲、破線は章の順序で、徒歩・交通経路や唐代道路ではない。
caption.en: The Big and Small Wild Goose Pagodas and Beilin at one scale. The Sui-Tang outer city is generalized; dashed joins show chapter order, not a walking path, transit route or Tang street.

p.src: Inside Beilin, do not assume that every stone has stood here since the Tang. The Kaicheng Classics and the Stone-Platform Classic of Filial Piety originally stood near the imperial academy in Tang Chang'an, then moved as the city contracted. In 1087, Lü Dazhong oversaw their transfer, with other major steles, to the present area. Beilin is therefore not a Tang gallery preserved in place. It is a history of relocation, re-erection, repair and rearrangement. Look for date and movement before the calligrapher's name, and a hall of masterpieces becomes an archive with a working life.

p.src: Completed in 837, the Kaicheng Classics survive on 114 stones and 228 faces, carrying twelve Confucian classics and more than 650,000 characters. Remember the totals once; do not attempt to read the whole first gallery. Choose one face. Follow how columns and sequence continue, then locate breaks, supplied characters and later recutting. The point is not the promotional claim that this is the world's heaviest book. It is an ordered reference text made durable enough for collation, while damage and repair remain visible in the material record.

p.src: Rubbing is how inscriptions on stone travelled beyond Beilin. Damp xuan paper is pressed gently into recessed carving; once settled, ink is built up with a cloth tamping pad. The surface darkens while the incised forms remain white, producing a portable impression. Rubbings carried letterforms and images widely, but repeated contact can abrade or stain vulnerable stone. The demonstration on this page shows paper, ink and hand position on a modern resin replica; it depicts no real object or museum activity. Never touch or rub an original unless the responsible institution has explicitly arranged a supervised replica exercise.

caption.zh: 现代树脂复制板上的传拓演示：宣纸贴合凹槽后逐层施墨。原碑是否允许接触，必须服从管理方规定。
caption.ja: 現代の樹脂製レプリカを使う拓本工程。宣紙を凹部へ密着させてから墨を置く。原碑への接触は管理者の規定に従う。
caption.en: Ink rubbing on a modern resin replica: xuan paper is settled into recesses before ink is applied. Any contact with an original remains subject to the institution's rules.

p.src: Erected in 781, the Jingjiao Stele recounts in Chinese the history of a Church of the East community in Tang China; Syriac names and titles appear below and along the sides. The monk Jingjing prepared the account and Lü Xiuyan supplied the calligraphy. One object therefore preserves a community's self-description, Chinese religious language and multilingual names. It is often called the Nestorian Stele, but Jingjiao Stele or Church of the East stele is more precise. It establishes presence, language and remembered history. One inscription cannot make the whole Tang period a frictionless age of tolerance.

p.src: Check reservations and access separately for all three places. As of 15 August 2026, Xi'an Museum uses timed real-name booking and normally closes on Tuesdays. Beilin also uses timed real-name booking, but its current official popup and footer publish conflicting hours, so this book does not reproduce either timetable. Check each booking page and same-day notice before leaving. Treat the public space around the Big Pagoda, temple admission and tower access as separate checks too. For a full day, work back from the earliest reservation and retain margins for security, walking, food and time seated.
